answer.rationale: The 18% spend cut mandate combined with a 14-day renewal deadline and 94% line utilization creates high pressure but also leverage. Memory c4 shows renegotiating at renewal recovered real margin through benchmarking; this is the most direct path to hit the cost target without operational risk. Memory c6 demonstrates that multi-year terms unlock volume pricing. Verifying c2 (low-cost vendor risk profile) and c4 (negotiation precedent) will confirm whether the incumbent can credibly meet the 18% reduction through better terms, or whether switching becomes necessary. The incumbent has proven reliable on integration (c1) and payment accuracy, but carries known SLA risk if made sole source under stress (c2). Negotiation preserves the ability to pivot to a second source or defer if the incumbent cannot move sufficiently on price, while keeping the critical line supplied. At 94% utilization, adding a second source is viable but delays cost recovery; deferral risks auto-expiry and tighter negotiating position next cycle.
